hints_text:
> The package structure should be acyclic, coupling between packages should be as low as possible.

100% agree. AntennaPod's code base has historically grown. Even model objects like the "FeedItem" class perform database queries. The code is a real mess in many places. Over the past 3 years, I have reworked quite a few monsterous classes but it is still far from being a good code structure.

Thanks for generating the dependency graph. It's even worse than what I thought. There hardly is any package that is not inside a cycle.

> are you almost happy with the (unit and integration) tests we have so far and spend the time mainly on new features?

I spend most of my time fixing bugs. Then new features. If there is still time left, I maybe do some code cleanup. I'm definitely not happy about the code structure, though. And I would probably have to spend less time doing bug fixes if the code had more tests.

A long-term goal would be to be able to separate the code base into multiple gradle modules (model, feed parser, media file parser, etc). I don't like the type of commits that touch everything at once because it creates conflicts in PRs and clutters the git history. So I think it would be best to start gradually and try to break some of the cycles. If one part (eg. the model) is completely free of dependencies, the files can be moved to a new gradle module (without code changes). I hope that this procedure then avoids completely breaking `git bisect`, which I use pretty much during bug fixing. Using gradle modules ensures that the graph stays acyclic because you simply can't access other gradle modules without thinking about it explicitly.

I am also wondering if the package structure in AntennaPod should be changed generally. Currently, classes are sorted by type (adapters, fragments, etc). Maybe it would be more clear if we sorted them by their use within the app (audio player: fragment + views + adapters. Queue: fragment + adapter, ...). The separation into `app` and `core` module has lead to quite a number of strange constructs with static variables, too. The core module was once used to allow creating white-labeled apps but that time is long gone.

If you are interested in helping to make the code structure more clean, that would be really appreciated!
I think rewriting it from scratch is far more efficient than breaking intertwined package cycles (if it's possible at all), in my experience.
That's what K-9 mail is doing since more than 2 years (and it is still not finished). In that time, their rating dropped significantly because users think that the project is abandoned. Also considering the fact that Google seems to rank apps based on their update behavior, a rewrite from scratch is not a path I want to go. We need to compete with commercial platforms that currently destroy the open podcast ecosystem instead of spending our time rewriting for the next 2 years.
After a rough review of the packages I can imagine to structure the AntennaPod software architecture in the following way:

![modules-refactoring](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46045854/99196982-c131b900-278f-11eb-9d42-a5cb0daa13be.png)

**Module :app**
Responsible for user interaction. Keeps all the packages it has now.

**Module :feed**
Provides an API for the :app module to read and modify feeds. Most of the non-ui business logic will be located here, mainly covers the current package `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.feed`.

**Module :eventbus**
Provides the EventBus (`org.greenrobot.eventbus.EventBus`), wraps the required access methods via non-static variables and methods.

**Module :storage**
Provides access to the feed data base, preferences and export/import. Mainly covers the current packages
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.export`
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.preferences`
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.storage`

**Module :communication**
Responsible for all external communication, e.g. downloading feed data, synchronization with gpodder.net. Mainly covers the current packages
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.service.download`
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.ssl`
- `de.danoeh.antennapod.core.sync`

I suggest to start with the base modules `:eventbus`, `:storage:`, and `:communication`. First, we add a new module and then refactor all usages step by step. Important requirements are to allow only downward dependencies, no upward dependencies, and to avoid static variables and methods to provide a good testability via unit tests without the usage of `mockStatic` and other dirty hacks.

Any comments on the approach? Anything else we should consider?

Shall we use Gradle modules to ensure only allowed dependencies? A more lightweight approach could be to check package dependencies via unit tests with e.g. [JDepend](https://github.com/clarkware/jdepend).
I think we should first try to separate a "model" module (Feed, FeedItem, Chapter). Then it should be possible to move feed parsing and chapter parsing to their own modules (both depending on the model). I have not compared your graph with your suggested module structure in more detail yet but I think even with your structure, we need a "model" module.

> Module :communication

This one could be hard to separate. It displays notifications which link to the main pages of the app. Not sure how that could be achieved if it does not have access to the main page. Child classes in the app module?

> Shall we use Gradle modules to ensure only allowed dependencies?

I think gradle modules would be nice.
> I think we should first try to separate a "model" module (Feed, FeedItem, Chapter).

A common data model is a very popular approach. But I want to emphasize a significant disadvantage: Most fields are kept optional (i.e. they can be null or empty) what makes the usage of the model error prone und complicated. So the model is like a superset of the fields required for several method calls. I collected some examples in AntennaPod:

* The methods `DBReader.getFeedList()` and `DBTasks.searchFeeds()` return a list of `Feed` objects with an empty `feed.items` list.
* The method `DBReader.loadDescriptionOfFeedItem(FeedItem item)` fills the fields `item.description` and `item.contentEncoded` which are `null` for all other method calls.
* Whenever the methods `DownloadRequester.downloadFeed(..., Feed feed, ...)` and `DownloadRequester.createRequest(FeedFile feed, ...)` are called, almost all fields in `feed` are `null` except the field `download_url` and a few others.
* The method `FeedHandler.parseFeed(Feed feed)` only uses the fields `download_url`, `file_url`, `type`, and `language` (only 4 of 23 fields).

Alternatively, a more slim approach could be to let every module provide its own model that only covers the fields supported by its API. For example, the classes `SyncService` and `GpodnetService` provide their own model classes in their `model` sub packages and thus perfectly fit to their API. If necessary, code using two modules needs to have some glue code to convert data from one model to another model.

What do you prefer?

>> Module :communication

> This one could be hard to separate. It displays notifications which link to the main pages of the app. Not sure how that could be achieved if it does not have access to the main page. Child classes in the app module?

I can imagine to use the `EventBus` to display notifications, this would technically uncouple the UI from the business logic in that case. But I haven't checked the details in that cases.

> I think gradle modules would be nice.

:+1:
Refactoring that code is really good idea. I would create at least 10 modules. One module should contain only few packages and every package should contain only few classes. Networking, persistence, view, event handling, model, utility, parsers etc.

I encourage to consider using libraries like Lombok which reduce boilerplate. I never used [Android Jetpack](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/getting-started) but its worth looking into.

There are also tools for automatic code refactoring, some built in Android Studio. That will iterate through classes and refactor them. 

Unrelated question, probably to @ByteHamster , is it common practice in android development to use internal android package name to put implemented classes in? For ex. `com.google.android.material.bottomsheet.ViewPagerBottomSheetBehavior` .
I suggest we roll up our sleeves and tackle changes to the code to make testing easier instead of talking about it.

I would expect any of those PRs to add a test for each refactoring.

Could we close this issue and get to work on it?😁
> Unrelated question, probably to @ByteHamster , is it common practice in android development to use internal android package name to put implemented classes in? For ex. com.google.android.material.bottomsheet.ViewPagerBottomSheetBehavior .

That's not a common practice but a hack to make it possible to extend a protected class
Sorry for the late reply @damoasda.

> Alternatively, a more slim approach could be to let every module provide its own model that only covers the fields supported by its API.

Most modules need access to the `Feed`, `FeedItem`, etc classes. I don't think those should be duplicated and converted for every single module. So I think as a first step, those could be separated (see also #4842). If that is done, we can already create modules for quite a few parts of the app (chapter parser, feed parser, OPML export, sync, maybe even database handling).
Many parts of the app need to start the main activity with different parameters (eg. widget, playback service, download service, sync). Any idea how to do that while still de-coupling the code? Currently, we use a ton of static variables in `ClientConfig` [that are then set from the app module](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/3f31764f58bdb8aab9182f3aa960ed827df42b9c/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/config/ClientConfigurator.java) but that is not really pretty.
That's the most difficult part of de-coupling the code. The class `ClientConfig` contains a collection of global references that might be dissolved in different steps:

1) **`ClientConfig.applicationCallbacks`** is used to provide the `Context` reference and to return a new `StorageErrorActivity` intent. Possible solution:
-- Hand over the `Context` reference as an additional parameter in the corresponding helper methods.
-- Move the method `applicationCallbacks.getStorageErrorActivity()` body into the method `StorageUtils.checkStorageAvailability()` as it is the only place that uses the method.

2) **`ClientConfig.downloadServiceCallbacks`** provides helper methods for the `DownloadService`.
Possible solution: Move `DownloadService` to app module.

3) **`ClientConfig.playbackServiceCallbacks`** provides a single method getPlayerActivityIntent() that is used by the `PlaybackService`.
Possible solution: Move `PlaybackService` to app module.

4) **`ClientConfig.automaticDownloadAlgorithm`** is only used by `DBTasks.autodownloadUndownloadedItems()` which is called by `DownloadService`, `DBWriter`, `ConnectivityActionReceiver`, and `PowerConnectionReceiver`. As both, the implementation and its usage are in  the `core` module, it should be easy to get rid of the field `ClientConfig.automaticDownloadAlgorithm`.

5) **`ClientConfig.castCallbacks`** is only used by `CastManager` for the "play" flavour to access a fragment.
Possible solution: Move `CastManager` to app module.
I had another idea for how to start the main activity (eg from DownloadService) that could work without moving all services to the same module. We could create an `intents` module that can send a specific intent. The intent is then picked up and interpreted by the main activity. I will try to come up with a proof-of-concept.
Very interesting. That sounds similar to the `EventBus` that could be an alternative.
EventBus only works when the app is already started but the idea is pretty much the same, yeah :)
I just tried to come up with a more detailed module structure. Looks a lot more cluttered than yours but I think it could be good to make it more detailed, so that the code is as decoupled as possible. (click to enlarge)

![modules](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5811634/131211095-7c38abec-09c8-4101-a929-23b6194a17a2.png)

What do you think?

Edit: Green modules are already done.
Wow, that's awesome! The graph is acyclic, the services are separated, and also the UI is split into several logic units.

Maybe we will identify more module candidates like ":storage:export" during the refactoring work or we will merge two modules again because the dependencies are too hard to dissolve. But that's fully ok and a concession to practice. :smile:

I'd be happy to start with your modularization approach.
Okay, nice :) Now that the `:app-start-intent` module is separated, we have to deal with the model module. Without that module, most others cannot be modularized. @widlok already started working on this in #4842 but the PR got a bit too big to handle. So I suggest to start with small steps and multiple individual PRs before actually creating the module. Some ideas for small chunks of work that could be done in individual PRs:

- [x] Remove `Cursor` related code from the model, as it is database specific
- [x] Decouple loading shownotes (I think this should be done after #3974 is merged)
- [x] Decouple loading chapter marks
- [x] Decouple saving FeedPreferences
- [x] `loadMetadata` in FeedMedia
- [x] `saveCurrentPosition` should be performed outside the model

Once all of that is done, I think we can move some model classes to their own module

@ByteHamster Hi, I would like to offer my help in the refactoring efforts. 
Let me know where I can start. 
For now, I have a few suggestions I thought i'd throw out there. 
1. Have designated developer be resposnbile for their own module(s).
2. I would like to be assigned to work on storage or may eveentbus.

Awesome!

First, we need to uncouple the model from the rest of the code. When that is done, we can start to do other modules (see https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/4661#issuecomment-778614258). If you want to do a PR like #4968 (but for another class), that would be great.

https://forum.antennapod.org/t/antennapod-2-3-0-release-notes/1047/1

@damoasda What tool did you use to generate the dependency graph?
I used [Graphviz](https://graphviz.org/).
And how did you analyze the code to get a Graphviz file?
I think I used the JDK tool jdeps. I found a note calling a command like this:
`jdeps --no-recursive -verbose:package --regex ^de.danoeh.antennapod..* --dot-output . core`
Thanks! So what I ended up doing was to run these commands

```
./gradlew assembleDebug
find -name "*.class" | xargs /usr/lib/jvm/default/bin/jdeps --dot-output __dependencies
cp __dependencies/summary.dot dependencies.dot
rm -r __dependencies
sed -i 's/\$[^\.]*\././g' dependencies.dot # Replaces inner classes with top class
```

Then I used `gephi` to (manually, repeatedly) remove nodes that have `indegree==0` or `outdegree==0`. This leaves us with a quite small number of 31 classes that are strongly connected. Once these dependencies are decoupled, the classes can be "peeled" to different modules without any dependency cycles.

A first decoupling of bloated utility classes (#6176) reduces the number of problematic classes down to only 19. The strongly connected classes give a quite nice overview about what needs to be done here.

![screenshot_233437](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5811634/199615526-46dcc074-6f42-47ff-ad14-8adf40ab9afa.png)
Making some more progress in #6176. We are down to 11 problematic classes.

![screenshot_232435](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5811634/199845990-340c2bb4-7f16-47c6-b7d1-561a58eb06b4.png)

Now it gets kind of hard, though. We have a ton of real dependencies here. Not just bloated utility classes. For example, the Synchronization feature needs access to the database to store the new state. At the same time, the database needs access to the sync service to upload possible changes.

Maybe we need to hide some classes behind an interface and then keep a reference to an actual implementation somewhere.That's not totally elegant, though. For the sync service, that should work rather easily, at least.
When this is done, we can create nice module graphs for developer documentation using this gradle plugin: https://github.com/iurysza/module-graph/tree/main

@keunes or @ByteHamster please assign to me, since I have the podcastindex namespace parsing done in #4933, I could tackle `podcast:transcript`
I have a a few suggestions for transcript related features I think  would be great to include in AntennaPod (originally mentioned in https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/5002):

1. Optionally including timestamps when copying from the trancsript. This would be helpful when using a noteapp to write down interesting segments from the podcast as it makes it easier to go back to the podcast an relisten to the particular segment.
2.  Having the transcript autoscroll as the episode is playing, so when switching to the transcript tab, the text is in the same position as the audio. This would facilitate notetaking while listening.
3. Searching the transcript. I am referring to searching within a single transcript , which would make it easier to find interesting segments (which in turn could be navigated to if combined with the below item).
4. Using the transcript for seeking in the audio (clicking sentences to jump to that position).

There are currently at least two podcast apps on iOS that provide some of these features, but none on Android as far as I know. Those apps are https://podcast9.com/ and https://www.airr.io/. They are labeling themselves as more educational / productive alternatives to regular podcast apps and their main value proposition is the ability to interact with and remember what you listen to as well as easily share your favorite bits with others.

A future item to consider which might be out of scope currently is to automatically create transcripts for episodes that don't provide it, e.g. using the live transcribe feature on phones where it is available.
Nice ideas 👍 My guess would be that # 4 wouldn't be too difficult. But for the others I guess we (the app) would need to receive the timestamps with the transcript I think - as I reckon it's not feasible for AP to automatically match the text with the audio. Do you know if transcripts typically have such timestamps?
Thanks @keunes ! I am not very experienced with podcast data and metadata, but I looked around a bit and it seems like at least some transcripts provide this. The [example used on the podcastindex API docs](https://podcastindex-org.github.io/docs-api/#get-/episodes/byid) page includes this segment:

```json
transcriptUrl: "https://mp3s.nashownotes.com/NA-1322-Captions.srt"
```

That srt file includes timestamps which look like this:

```srt
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:05,340
Pull my mask over my nose. Adam
Curry John C Dvorak, Thursday,

2
00:00:05,340 --> 00:00:09,030
February 18 2021. This is your
award winning media

3
00:00:09,030 --> 00:00:13,380
assassination Episode 13. This
is no agenda.

...
```

I am not sure how common it is, but at least it exists.

A complimentary approach that is less robust but does not rely on external data could be to match the relative position of sentences in the transcript with the relative time of the audio file (when no timestamps are available). Even if this was only able to generate precision to the minute, I think it would be helpful for most items I mentioned above. For some, like the scrolling text, it would probably perform quite well since so much of the transcript would be shown on the screen that the matched position does not have to be exact. It would probably benefit from calculating the relative audio position without silences (I noted that there is already an option in AP to skip these when listening).

I like to add an idea mentioned in the issue above: **hide empty tabs** - that could be empty transcripts and especially nonexistent chapters, if only one tab remains the tablayout itself should probably be hidden.

I think thats a sensible solution, to not crowd the AudioPlayer with empty tabs and require to user to swipe a thousand times to get to the desired tab, makes the UX clearer :)
@tonytamsf Any idea how to implement the data store? Downloading all transcripts of all episodes could result in a huge amount of text to be stored. We already have the problem that the database is pretty big. I think it would be better to only store the URLs and then load the transcript when actually viewing the transcript page in AntennaPod. We could enable caching with okhttp to reduce the number of web requests.

Hi, really exciting times for AntennaPod and Podcsting in general. I've been doing some research about the use of transcript in the Podcasting 2.0 namespace.
- I've found that even these mime types being equivalent `text/srt` `application/srt` `application/x-subrip` most player don't support all 3, so in in a "test" feed I declare all for the same file. 
- SRT is the most used format, then JSON, VTT and TXT (but these are usually full transcripts, not subtitle with parsable timecodes)

In case is useful, I have a feed with different options of redirect/hosting with different formats and mime-types if you want to test different edge cases, as discussed here : https://github.com/podverse/podverse-web/issues/1168#issuecomment-1695231077
Probably the redirect / hosting part is no problem here as that part was for testing CORS in different web players. (Gitlab Pages works best with web players than Archive if something is interested)

```
Episode 16
Op3+ archive.org + vtt only

Episode 15
Op3+ gitlab + vtt only

Episode 09
Op3 + gitlab + vtt
Op3 + archive + srt

Episode 08 (without OP3)
Gitlab + vtt
Archive + srt

Episode Episode 00
Op3 + gitlab + vtt/srt

All others
OP3 + archive + vtt/srt

2. SRT - these are accurate to about 32 characters, and therefore the timing isn't as perfect as it could be. [It works like this](https://www.steno.fm/show/917393e3-1b1e-5cef-ace4-edaa54e1f810/episode/YTQ2OWE5ZmQtMzVlOC00MDNhLWIzMDUtZGEyNmU3MDE1ZjBh).

I have a test build of how we can display transcripts in 2 lines of text on the player screen.

It works for JSON (word by word) or SRT (a few seconds of text).

The way I am able to nicely display the transcript is as follows

- join up segments of text at least one second, most json segments are less than 1 second
- string together N segments and display them on the two lines of TextView, which has support for ellipses 
- when I detect an ellipse in the TexView, which means words are cut off at the end, start trimming words from the end until the display does not have ellipses. 
- move the words that have been ellipsed to the next segment, and  trimming a little more to get some buffer
- calculate a reasonable (percentage of words trimmed) new start time of the next segment 
- display the text sync to the position of the audio
- move to the next segment

# Feature description
Some podcasts include text transcript using `podcast:transcipt`

**Suggested solution**:
Display transcript and sync it with the audio.

hints_text:
@keunes or @ByteHamster please assign to me, since I have the podcastindex namespace parsing done in #4933, I could tackle `podcast:transcript`
I have a a few suggestions for transcript related features I think  would be great to include in AntennaPod (originally mentioned in https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/5002):

1. Optionally including timestamps when copying from the trancsript. This would be helpful when using a noteapp to write down interesting segments from the podcast as it makes it easier to go back to the podcast an relisten to the particular segment.
2.  Having the transcript autoscroll as the episode is playing, so when switching to the transcript tab, the text is in the same position as the audio. This would facilitate notetaking while listening.
3. Searching the transcript. I am referring to searching within a single transcript , which would make it easier to find interesting segments (which in turn could be navigated to if combined with the below item).
4. Using the transcript for seeking in the audio (clicking sentences to jump to that position).

There are currently at least two podcast apps on iOS that provide some of these features, but none on Android as far as I know. Those apps are https://podcast9.com/ and https://www.airr.io/. They are labeling themselves as more educational / productive alternatives to regular podcast apps and their main value proposition is the ability to interact with and remember what you listen to as well as easily share your favorite bits with others.

A future item to consider which might be out of scope currently is to automatically create transcripts for episodes that don't provide it, e.g. using the live transcribe feature on phones where it is available.
Nice ideas 👍 My guess would be that # 4 wouldn't be too difficult. But for the others I guess we (the app) would need to receive the timestamps with the transcript I think - as I reckon it's not feasible for AP to automatically match the text with the audio. Do you know if transcripts typically have such timestamps?
Thanks @keunes ! I am not very experienced with podcast data and metadata, but I looked around a bit and it seems like at least some transcripts provide this. The [example used on the podcastindex API docs](https://podcastindex-org.github.io/docs-api/#get-/episodes/byid) page includes this segment:

```json
transcriptUrl: "https://mp3s.nashownotes.com/NA-1322-Captions.srt"
```

That srt file includes timestamps which look like this:

```srt
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:05,340
Pull my mask over my nose. Adam
Curry John C Dvorak, Thursday,

2
00:00:05,340 --> 00:00:09,030
February 18 2021. This is your
award winning media

3
00:00:09,030 --> 00:00:13,380
assassination Episode 13. This
is no agenda.

...
```

I am not sure how common it is, but at least it exists.

A complimentary approach that is less robust but does not rely on external data could be to match the relative position of sentences in the transcript with the relative time of the audio file (when no timestamps are available). Even if this was only able to generate precision to the minute, I think it would be helpful for most items I mentioned above. For some, like the scrolling text, it would probably perform quite well since so much of the transcript would be shown on the screen that the matched position does not have to be exact. It would probably benefit from calculating the relative audio position without silences (I noted that there is already an option in AP to skip these when listening).

I like to add an idea mentioned in the issue above: **hide empty tabs** - that could be empty transcripts and especially nonexistent chapters, if only one tab remains the tablayout itself should probably be hidden.

I think thats a sensible solution, to not crowd the AudioPlayer with empty tabs and require to user to swipe a thousand times to get to the desired tab, makes the UX clearer :)
@tonytamsf Any idea how to implement the data store? Downloading all transcripts of all episodes could result in a huge amount of text to be stored. We already have the problem that the database is pretty big. I think it would be better to only store the URLs and then load the transcript when actually viewing the transcript page in AntennaPod. We could enable caching with okhttp to reduce the number of web requests. 
> @tonytamsf Any idea how to implement the data store? Downloading all transcripts of all episodes could result in a huge amount of text to be stored. We already have the problem that the database is pretty big. I think it would be better to only store the URLs and then load the transcript when actually viewing the transcript page in AntennaPod. We could enable caching with okhttp to reduce the number of web requests.

I like your idea, there is no need to store transcription.  Depending on the user, they may not want to be downloading transcript using mobile data, so we might have to get user consent to use mobile to download transcript.
Why not storing transcript on file text on device? Same way episodes are stored. They would be removed along with episodes and it would allow to make them available like episodes are.

Edit :
And it won't clutter database except maybe to put a flag to know there is transcript downloaded. I am not sure it's even needed as all logics would be parallel to what is done for downloaded episodes.
Sounds like a good idea. When streaming, users need a data connection anyways. When downloading, we can download the transcripts, too. :+1:
> Why not storing transcript on file text on device?

I'm just wondering: this wouldn't hinder 'processing' the info (esp. timestamps, for # 4 in OP).

> When downloading, we can download the transcripts, too

Just to throw an idea out: couldn't this be done, but then in the db? As in, download & store in db when episode is downloaded; remove from dB when file is deleted? (Don't know if this would have any actual benefit, see above).
I don't think storing and using text files would cause any problem : it is what video player does with srt files for subtitles.
Storing it in the database but only for downloaded episodes should work :) Then we don't need to store the file path, we can just store the transcript directly.
Don't know if you saw how Podverse implemented transcript with search. For reference there is a video of what they did : https://twitter.com/Podverse/status/1413642917760184325?s=19

IMHO about their screen : 
- I would prefer timecode on left side and with a smaller font and using grey as text color. So time code would be there but won't distract your eyes when reading transcription
- I wouldn't separate block like they did. It's like there is an empty line beetween each segment which is annoying when reading
Thanks for sharing that @Matth7878!

> I would prefer timecode on left side and with a smaller font and using grey as text color

Fully agree

> I wouldn't separate block like they did

I understand your point, but we can't really merge sentences that are separated into two blocks I think:
* we don't know where we can stitch parts together, and where a hard enter should be kept (in the interface). If there's no whitespace, it might still be complicated to read:
![Schermafdruk van 2021-07-11 10-45-14](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11229646/125188759-38432280-e235-11eb-89f0-e0ce24a2ffff.png)
* if we do stitch together the sentences, there might be a situation where one line on the screen covers three lines in the transcript file. Then we can only display the first timestamp, which can be problematic in some cases (e.g. when there is a line with `[silence]` that takes a minute - you wouldn't be able to jump to the bit after the silence).

Any thoughts about the support of all 4 content types in the `<podcast:transcript>` tag?

Spec: https://github.com/Podcastindex-org/podcast-namespace/blob/main/transcripts/transcripts.md

* HTML - this format has no or limited timecode - I recommend that we ignore this
* JSON - Much more flexible - we should fully support this, I'm searching for sample podcast that use this format (not seeing it yet)
* SRT - great for video or audio, max number of lines 2, max chars 32 - I recommend we support this fully
* WebVTT - for HTML on the web, I recommend we don't support this

Example: https://podnews.net/rss

```
<podcast:transcript url="https://podnews.net/audio/podnews230310.mp3.vtt" type="text/vtt" />
<podcast:transcript url="https://podnews.net/audio/podnews230310.mp3.srt" type="application/srt" />
<podcast:transcript url="https://podnews.net/audio/podnews230310.mp3.txt" type="text/plain" />
<podcast:transcript url="https://podnews.net/audio/podnews230310.mp3.srt" type="application/x-subrip" rel="captions" />
```

It looks like Podnews also provides `text/pain` which is not in the Podcast 2.0 spec

@jamescridland I am a loyal listener of Podnews, is there a reason you don't have JSON version of `podcast:transcript`?  

Example: Podcasting 2.0 https://feeds.podcastindex.org/pc20.xml

Hi, really exciting times for AntennaPod and Podcsting in general. I've been doing some research about the use of transcript in the Podcasting 2.0 namespace.
- I've found that even these mime types being equivalent `text/srt` `application/srt` `application/x-subrip` most player don't support all 3, so in in a "test" feed I declare all for the same file. 
- SRT is the most used format, then JSON, VTT and TXT (but these are usually full transcripts, not subtitle with parsable timecodes)

In case is useful, I have a feed with different options of redirect/hosting with different formats and mime-types if you want to test different edge cases, as discussed here : https://github.com/podverse/podverse-web/issues/1168#issuecomment-1695231077
Probably the redirect / hosting part is no problem here as that part was for testing CORS in different web players. (Gitlab Pages works best with web players than Archive if something is interested)

```
Episode 16
Op3+ archive.org + vtt only

Episode 15
Op3+ gitlab + vtt only

Episode 09
Op3 + gitlab + vtt
Op3 + archive + srt

Episode 08 (without OP3)
Gitlab + vtt
Archive + srt

Episode Episode 00
Op3 + gitlab + vtt/srt

All others
OP3 + archive + vtt/srt
```
A problem that I've found with some player, in case you want to take it into account, is that if there is first a transcript tag with a file that doesn't work, some player won't try the next tag that would work.

Feed:
https://kdeexpress.gitlab.io/feed

**TL;NR**

I would prioritize SRT parsing, then JSON and if there is no much trouble VTT given the similarities with SRT. 
For `text/html` and `text/plain` I would either show a new screen with all the text just assuming that is the full transcript to read or just offer a link to be open in the web browser.
I'd jump in here and say two things:

The accurate stat is [contained here](https://stats.podcastindex.org/hourly_counts.json) - which at the time of writing is: 

>    "feedsWithTranscripts": 38,255
>    "episodesWithTranscripts": 1,379,606

There's obviously a chicken and egg scenario with support. If AntennaPod supports transcripts, it would be a significant benefit to podcasting as a whole, but also to the uptake of this feature. But you'll get considerable promotion when this is launched. (I will, as one guarantee, give you a headline story in Podnews.)

Secondly; might I suggest you ideally support these in this format:

1. JSON - this is accurate to the word level, and allows [this kind of highlighted transcript](https://www.steno.fm/show/9b024349-ccf0-5f69-a609-6b82873eab3c/episode/aHR0cHM6Ly9wb2RuZXdzLm5ldC91cGRhdGUvZ2Vuei1mYXN0ZXN0LWdyb3dpbmc=), where the individual word being said is highlighted on screen. That also allows you to lay out closed-captions in a very bespoke way - allowing you to properly wordwrap them. It also allows more features in future like clipping, where you could highlight a word or sentence, and have the app specifically clip that accurately.

2. SRT - these are accurate to about 32 characters, and therefore the timing isn't as perfect as it could be. [It works like this](https://www.steno.fm/show/917393e3-1b1e-5cef-ace4-edaa54e1f810/episode/YTQ2OWE5ZmQtMzVlOC00MDNhLWIzMDUtZGEyNmU3MDE1ZjBh). 

I'd, frankly, not support TXT or HTML unless you really want to - my suspicion is that these are relatively poorly supported anyway. But it doesn't seem like a heavy lift to simply open these in a webview. (I'm also very unclear if anyone is using VTT.)

I hope that helps a bit!

There are a number of issues around incomplete downloads but more than what to do about them I should first point out that they are invisible and take up space. This could happen when the app crashes while downloading or the storage fills up. Unless one downloads frequently from a relatively short backlog list of episodes and does one thing at a time, it's easy to lose track of what had been attempted. I imagine that over time these episodes add up to wasted space. I know that space is wasted because resuming a download does not start from scratch. Maybe these clear periodically but that would be also the wrong approach because the user could be roaming (data cost) or intended to hear something and the time spent spotting it again would be a waste.

The main issue is that there is hidden state. It's not obvious if any downloads are incomplete, and no easy / actionable list of such.

### Suggested solution

I see that there is a "Download Log" button at the top right, that I didn't notice before. I cannot tell if that would have helped because if the app doesn't crash, or the target space fills-up, things just continue downloading automatically. This log is fine showing everything, but the main issue as I see it is failed partial downloads that have started and are now incomplete. Several solutions are possible, all addressing the same issue in different ways, any one of the 1-3, and especially 2 or 3 would be great to have:

1. a different icon for incomplete downloads as a visual cue to hit download again
2. add a separate button (next to the Download Log button) with a list of just such downloads and with two options for each item -- resume or delete
3. if a separate list is undesirable, perhaps add a filter for the various things in the log -- a second row of toggle buttons (union of category sets) or a menu (all vs select single category) -- my particular interest being the Incomplete category (all options should fit on a single line)
4. Finally, perhaps there could be a summary about how much space incomplete downloads take up and a button to delete all of them (this is a nice-to-have that would make the #2 solution even better)

All of the above are complementary, some perhaps slightly easier. What's best would depend on the aesthetic preferences of the maintainers.

The title of this ticket doesn't seem to ask for what I want, but another issue said that *this* issue is tracking a new feature to automatically retry downloading podcasts after failure.

 * https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues/5869#issuecomment-1119979906

### Background Context

I don't have a SIM card, and I live in a city where wifi is abundant, yet spotty.

As I walk around the city on any given day, my Android phone will sit in my pocket and scan for wifi connections. Usually, when I do check my phone at some point after walking around, I notice that I have a bunch of unread messages on WhatsApp. That's because WhatsApp detected that I had internet and **automatically downloaded all my messages during the brief ~60 seconds during which I was walking past a wifi hotspot. This is great!**

Moreover, once I notice the messages, I can proceed to write back replies, even if I don't have Internet at this time. In WhatsApp, this works fine. Whatsapp will just queue up the messages for sending. **The next time I walk by a wifi hotspot, it will blast all my previously-failed-to-send messages out to the Internet. This is great UX!**

#### Expected Behaviour

A lot of the grocery stores that I shop at have free wifi. As you walk around the store, the wiif quality varies from 5% packet loss to 100% packet loss. Even though the Internet is shitty, AntennaPod should be capable of gracefully handling downloads on such connections in the background *without any user interaction whatsoever*.

**I expect to be able to walk into a grocery store that has free wifi with my phone in my pocket, do my shopping, and walk out with new podcasts downloaded. I should not have to take my phone out of my pocket for this to happen**

I realize that achieving this is non-trivial, but it absolutely can be done. My Android phone will automatically connect to the wifi network. AntennaPod should be able to get notified about the change of network status and immediately begin attempting to download podcasts in the background. As I move to the back of the store to buy almond milk (and packet loss rises from 5% to 100%), AntennaPod should handle this. As I move back to the front of the store to the cash register (and packet loss drops from 100% to 5%), AntennaPod should automatically retry the downloads, [picking-up where they were left-off](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Range_requests).

Add option to switch a- & descending sort order for Inbox
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function for [open](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues) **and** [closed](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) issues to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.

### App version

2.7.1

### Where did you get the app from

F-Droid

### Problem you may be having, or feature you want

It would be **so** nice to have, at last, the **option of an inbox in chronological order**.

I am coming back to Antennapod after a hiatus and now I remember the main reason I left. **The queue is sortable, but for some reason the inbox is not.** This seems verging on bug-like but I guess it's just an oversight. I am well aware that only a minority of crazy people like to do things in chronological order.

Please allow me a digression on the form of a good-faith rant about sort order. Rant begins HERE. _I don't get it. Why would anyone want to deal with an inbox from bottom to top? What am I not understanding? Do we read books from bottom to top? Lists? Timetables? Anything at all? The podcasts arrived in an order - chronological order. Perhaps they are news, in which case the most recent ones are dependent on previous ones for context. Perhaps they are episodes in a series, or chapters in an audiobook. It seems to me so obviously inefficient to be working through a list backwards (or scrolling upwards) that I keep thinking I must have missed something. Have I? I suspect not, but it's a serious question._ Rant ends.

Gmail does this too BTW. Impossible to sort in chronological order - newest first, take it or leave it (but oddly the Conversation View is chronological). I don't use evil Gmail but Antennapod is a great FOSS project, probably even the best podcast client out there.

### Suggested solution

An option to sort the Inbox into chronological order.

For those weirdos among us who like to deal with podcasts in the same order they dropped, this "feature" would be very, very much appreciated. Thanks for considering.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

_No response_
hints_text:
Hi @Friptick,

Two thoughts:
* No need for a rant – we also accept feature requests if they simply make sense ;-) (Also: you're speaking of 'at last' – sounds like you should've made this feature request earlier instead of cropping up frustration ^^)
* The inbox _is_ in chronological order, just not of the sort you would like to see (oldest first).

I don't see a reason not to introduce a 'Reverse sort order' option for the Inbox, behind the three dots in the top bar.
Thanks.

>No need for a rant

Rest assured the rant was not directed at you, it was directed at the whole world. :)

>sounds like you should've made this feature request earlier instead of cropping up frustration ^^

I was one of the users who campaigned for the sort options on the queue. I guess I just ran out of energy for campaigning.

>The inbox is in chronological order

No it's not. It is in reverse-chronological order. It's the innovation introduced by [blogging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog) ("Posts are typically displayed in reverse chronological order so that the most recent post appears first"). That's fine when you have one new blog post to read each time you visit a web page. It never made any sense for a feed of 100 items where (1) you don't want to miss anything, (2) "mark as read" exists, and (3) content is inter-related. But what do I know, hey? Nobody else is complaining, you're right. :) Seriously, I would so love to hear a counter-argument one day.

>I don't see a reason not to introduce a 'Reverse sort order' option for the Inbox, behind the three dots in the top bar.

Yep exactly, that was where I was surprised not to find it.

If I had any experience at all with Android dev, I promise I would do this myself and submit a PR.

Thanks.

When the text color is black on black, the podcast creator messed up their feed. Stripping text colors could lead to unexpected behavior when creators deliberately use text colors.

@keunes Do you think we should break (rare) valid use-cases to work around some other publishers messing up their feed? Apparently other apps do that as well. No strong opinion here.
> Stripping text colors could lead to unexpected behavior when creators deliberately use text colors.

I'd note that nobody else having noticed yet (assumption on my part, but I believe not unreasonable), may also point towards the existence of a de-facto standard for podcatchers not to render colors in descriptions.

Another relevant element, is podcasts being an off-shoot, built on top of RSS; off the top of my mind, the custom of displaying the original page in the reader has largely left room to rendering the content in a way that is consistent with the appearance of the RSS reader itself.

With that said, however, there are certainly RSS readers that offer the option to switch between the two modes of presentation, though IME this seems largely confined to desktop readers, as the Android readers I've seen simply offer the chance of an integrated look or rendering the content through what is considered an external component, or the browser app.
> Do you think we should break (rare) valid use-cases to work around some other publishers messing up their feed? Apparently other apps do that as well. No strong opinion here.

Yeah, I think it's fine to strip colours. (Better to protect usability than edge use cases identified by podcasters. And frankly I think it's more likely that podcasters mess up accidentally than use colours deliberately and correctly.)

Good first issue?

problem_statement: Remove restriction on playback history length ### Checklist - [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request. - [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. - [X] This request contains only one single feature, **not** a list of multiple (related) features. ### App version 2.4.2 ### Where did you get the app from F-Droid ### Problem you may be having, or feature you want The playback history has a fixed length of 50. I use "playback history" to review how long it's been since I listened to various podcasts, so that I can try to evenly sample my podcasts (e.g. roughly follow a cycle of ABCABCABC). I listen to enough podcasts that often a 50 episode history is not enough, and I'd like to configure the history to be longer, or even unlimited. ### Suggested solution I recommend adding a `Playback History Length` preference, under the `User Interface` menu (I am not particularly tied to any of these names). ### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details Preference screen: Modifying: It could be the case that -1 == "unlimited", as I've got it in the current implementation: Alternatively we could set the playback history limit to a fixed number and then add a checkbox for "no limit". This is a nicer user experience, but maybe can wait for a second pass while the "-1" workaround is available? *EDIT*: I've updated the title to reflect that we're removing the restriction rather than making the value configurable.
hints_text:
I don't think this should be a user setting. We have more than enough settings already. The only reason for limiting the length is that loading all would have bad performance. Internally, the list is unlimited and simply sorts all episodes by their "last played" date. Instead, the screen could get lazy loading like the "all episodes" screen.
Fine by me, I can adjust the implementation accordingly if that's how you'd like to do it.
>  I use "playback history" to review how long it's been since I listened to various podcasts, so that I can try to evenly sample my podcasts

Would the following help?

1. Set Subscription Order to "Sort by Counter".
2. Set your Subscription Counter to "Number of New Episodes"

Assuming comparable release schedules among all podcasts you're subscribed to, you should find the neglected ones rising to the top.
> Would the following help?
> 
>     1. Set Subscription Order to "Sort by Counter".
> 
>     2. Set your Subscription Counter to "Number of New Episodes"
> 
> 
> Assuming comparable release schedules among all podcasts you're subscribed to, you should find the neglected ones rising to the top.

Unfortunately no, my workflow depends heavily on the actual order that I listened to the episodes in. The assumption of comparable release schedules doesn't really hold, and there are many other ways in which number of new episodes is not a good proxy for what I want.

#5244 would be a big help to me (even in a world where playback history length is unlimited), but @ByteHamster's solution seems best and easiest.

> Fine by me, I can adjust the implementation accordingly if that's how you'd like to do it.

That would be great :) It's probably not completely easy to do, though. Maybe you can make the class extend the episode list fragment, like on the "all episodes" page.

problem_statement:
Sharing media URL no longer possible after combined episode sharing
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] If the bug only to occurs with a certain podcast, I will include the URL of that podcast.

### App version

2.5.0

### Where did you get the app from

Google Play

### Android version

original Android 12

### Device model

Pixel 3a

### First occurred

Since update to 2.5.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. choose an episode.
2. Long-press the episode and select "share".
3. keep the default selection "share episode".
4. Select as share target an app which can handle media files, such as [Yatse](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.leetzone.android.yatsewidgetfree) or [BubbleUPNP](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bubblesoft.android.bubbleupnp).
5. Note with the combined episode sharing as changed in #5626 Yatse sends the episode info to Kodi but Kodi doesn't start playing because the first URL doesn't point to the media file, but to the episode website.


### Expected behaviour

Before the changes in #5626, it was possible to send the media URL of a podcast episode to any App which is capable of receiving media URLs and playing them back on i.e. a DLNA media player or media center software such as Kodi.
I was using the episode media URL sharing almost daily to play Podcast episodes on my Kodi mediacenter.

### Current behaviour

Now antennapod sends two URLs in the shared data, where the first one isn't the media URL, but the URL to the episode website. When the recipient tries to play it, it's not working of course.

Please bring back the separate sharing of episode media URLS, as the combined episode sharing in its current implementation completely broke this workflow.

### Logs

_No response_
hints_text:
Does Kodi always play the first URL or does it only play when there is one single URL? If it plays the first URL, we could simply switch the two URLs in the text.

cc @keunes who requested #5339
I did a few tests:
- After swapping the media URL and episode website URL, sharing with kodi via Yatse works again.
- Although sharing with BubbleUPNP still doesn't work, because BubbleUPNP seems to parse only the the first line. The separate media URL sharing consisted of a single line, which is why it was working there.
- VLC and Hifi Cast aren't working, though they weren't working before, as they can handle only URLS if they are not prepended with other text such as the episode title.

Please at least swap the media and episode website URLs so that Podcast episodes can be played on Kodi again. This would however still not make sharing work with BubbleUPNP again.
 
An optimal solution would be to share only the media URL, not surrounded by informational text.

Can confirm, here's the podcast link that I sent to my computer through KDE connect after unsuccessfully trying to share it to my Kodi device:
```

War Nerd Radio — Subscriber Feed: Radio War Nerd EP 322 — Chechen Wars, Pt. 2: 1722-1991 + Ukraine-Russia War Update

Episode webpage: http://exiledonline.com/45wn84klrz/?name=rwn_ep_322_032422_v31.mp3

Media file: http://exiledonline.com/45wn84klrz/media/rwn_ep_322_032422_v31.mp3
```

Only the Media File link works on Kodi after sending the link manually by using a desktop Kodi remote.
This change was introduced to simplify the UX & UI for users trying to share an episode with others. While I understand and see your use-case, that's a 'side benefit' of the functionality.

I'm not really a fan of putting the media file first, as for person-to-person sharing the webpage in most cases is most relevant. Would there be other ways in which the media could be started on Kodi, or a UPNP server?
Would it be possible to implement this as an option in the settings? There are of course other ways to play these media on Kodi, but they are comparatively very awkward and require multiple steps, different for each podcast/platform.

With AntennaPod I used to be able to have all my podcast subscriptions as a list that I could quickly share to play on my DIY Kodi jukebox over my network with two taps. That was incredibly handy without having to hunt for the specific media file every time and/or have the right addons for specific podcast services installed on Kodi - and these tend to be rather buggy.
Older issues show the demand of podcast episodes on external devices, (see #961, #2256,  and #2920.) Antennapods google Cast support is a convinient solution for this, although Google Cast is a proprietary protocol and not usable by other media players not certified by Google, while the integration is particularly not possible with FOSS media players.

Media URL sharing was a maybe less convinient, but more generic solution for playing Podcast episodes on external devices. Loosing this just because of cosmetical reasons would be very frustrating.

Getting the separate media URL sharing back as a opt-in feature would be okay for me. DLNA integration as proposed in #961 would be awesome of course, but also a lot of work probably.

@keunes I don't really see other options than reverting the change or switching the URLs. Being able to share to Kodi is a pretty nice feature that we would otherwise lose.
There's also positive feedback about the simplified sharing: https://fe.disroot.org/objects/cf0449b5-3114-4f6c-9871-6fff0d64f529

Maybe (for now) we can have two options, but different than what was there before:
* For social (as is)
* For media receiver (only media URL, so that VLC etc work as well)
* Media file (if downloaded)

With an a tickbox for 'don't ask again' (for such settings we should have a 'reset tips & don't asks' option, or an 'advanced' category in the settings to allow setting these kind of nitty-gritty things).

In the long run it'd be great to have DLNA as @henningoschwald mentioned if that works well with Kodi, or https://github.com/MayaPosch/NymphCast which looks really cool (if/when it [integrates with Kodi](https://github.com/MayaPosch/NymphCast/issues/32)).
> There's also positive feedback about the simplified sharing

Interesting

> Maybe (for now) we can have two options, but different than what was there before

Sounds good

> With an a tickbox for 'don't ask again'

Sharing media file vs sharing a link are fundamentally different things that one might want to do both. If we added a checkbox, users would forget that they set it and then complain that they cannot do the other method of sharing. So I would not add that.
Just want to say I totally support @henningoschwald's request. I, too, used to send the media file link to Kodi and was very happy with that feature.

My suggestion is to make the sharing popup look similar as before, with different options, for example:
- Share description text and URLs
- Share website URL
- Share media URL

The additional tap required by this did not bother me before. But if you think it is one tap too much, you could add an option in the settings to select a default sharing mode.
> Sharing media file vs sharing a link are fundamentally different things that one might want to do both

True, except if one doesn't use such media receivers :)

I'm thinking that rather than adjusting the 'share' menu, this functionality could be re-introduced at a higher level: at the same level as 'Share' add option 'Send to media receiver'. This also makes sense given that both things are fundamentally different things.
> The additional tap required by this did not bother me before.

The dialog already remembers whether or not you ticked the "include position" box. It could also remember which option is selected, so everyone just needs one single tap.

> this functionality could be re-introduced at a higher level

Hmm, our long-press menu items already are pretty full. Also, I am not sure if we should actively promote this as a feature by calling it "Send to media receiver" as it undermines one of the main points of AntennaPod (keeping track of the position and playback state). I would rather keep this as some kind of "unofficial" feature, just like we unofficially support non-podcast RSS.
Ok, so then conclusion is: adjust sharing screen to the following:

- `For social` [as is]
- `For media receiver` [only media URL, so that VLC etc work as well]
- `Media file` [available only if downloaded]

If 'Media file' is selected, then 'Include: Playback position' should be disabled.

When playing around with the sharing, I also noticed these small points of improvement:
* When sharing a podcast that I didn't (start) listen(ing) to, the option 'Playback position' is active, even though there's no point in having the choice in this situation. But I guess it can stay this way -- there's no real benefit to disabling the choice either.
* It's a bit odd to have a newline between 'Include' and '[ ] Playback position. It made sense before I guess because there were multiple options, but now there isn't it'd look neater if there's just one checkbox with the label 'Include playback position'.
* The share menu label has a horizontal ellipsis, which I think is a leftover from the time when there was still a sub-menu (`Share…`). Would be nicer to remove it.
* The sharing of *podcasts* (rather than episodes) still has a sub-menu, with the options 'Website address' and 'Podcast feed URL'. This, too, I think could be simplified by combining both URLs in one.

hints_text:
Hi and thank you for writing this issue!

It looks like you did not follow our issue template. In case you accidentally deleted the template, you can find the version for bug reports [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/develop/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md) and the version for feature requests [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/develop/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md). Please copy the matching template and then edit your post to follow the template. Please also make sure to use the [search function](https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/issues?q=is%3Aissue) to look for open **and** closed issues about the same topic.

In order to properly deal with the issue, we need the information requested in the template. Please note that dealing with duplicate issues and asking users to follow the issue template takes away a lot of time from the developers. That time can then not be spent to actually implement features.
Hi @vitaly-zdanevich
What do you mean with 'bright image'? Do you mean it's too bright when using the dark theme?

I thought of updating the issue title to "Local files image blurred & too bright for dark theme" to clarify a bit what you mean.
Yes, the image is too bright for night.
@ByteHamster If I were to provide an SVG, would AP be able to use that? (So that it's sharp whatever the screen res)
Unfortunately not. The image loading code for covers does not work with SVG. Another problem I noticed with the default image is that it uses the same blue color for both light and dark theme, even though the accent color is different in the themes. Maybe we should use gray instead.
> Another problem I noticed with the default image is that it uses the same blue color for both light and dark theme, even though the accent color is different in the themes.

Not sure what you mean - isn't it a single blue-and-white image used for both themes? Or is it something like white-on-transparent where the 'transparent' is (supposed to be) replaced by a theme colour?

Not a huge fan of grey. Could we not have two image versions, used depending on the theme?
> Not sure what you mean - isn't it a single blue-and-white image used for both themes?

Yes, it is - but that's the problem. We use a different accent color in both themes.

> Could we not have two image versions, used depending on the theme?

That would be pretty hard to add, I think. We would probably need to change all locations where we display images.

---

@vitaly-zdanevich Did you know that you can just create a file named `Folder.png` in the local folder, which will then be used as the cover image?
> but that's the problem. We use a different accent color in both themes.

As in: the problem is that the blue in the cover image is different from the blueue that is used for elements like the playback position indicator & the NEW label?

> white-on-transparent where the 'transparent' is (supposed to be) replaced by a theme colour

Would that be an option?
> As in: the problem is that the blue in the cover image is different from the blueue that is used for elements like the playback position indicator & the NEW label?

Yes. Also, different from the seek bar that is displayed directly below the image.

>> white-on-transparent where the 'transparent' is (supposed to be) replaced by a theme colour
> Would that be an option?

Hmm, not really. Would need changes to all places where we use images, too.

> Could we not have two image versions, used depending on the theme?

I just noticed that there is another option. We could switch the theme-based image when refreshing the local feed. That way, it will not be perfect and you can run into cases where it still uses the wrong one until the next refresh but it should be rather easy to implement.
> We could switch the theme-based image when refreshing the local feed.

I think that'd be a great improvement already.

How big (pixels) should the file be, to look good also on the higher end phones?
So... I had a look at the code again and noticed that AntennaPod relies on the exact values of the fallback image in some places. So I think the more clean way to implement automatic theme switching would be to write a Glide loader (just like the one for `EmbeddedChapterImage.java`). This has the advantage that we can actually use vectors and that switching automatically will work. The disadvantage is that it is pretty much work to implement and for me, it's not a priority. Maybe someone else wants to write the Glide loader. Before that is done, I don't think we need to design the image already.
> the more clean way to implement automatic theme switching would be to write a Glide loader (just like the one for `EmbeddedChapterImage.java`)

Would that warrant a separate issue?
Nope, it's just for loading the default local files image :)

At least in my opinion the correct solution would be for owncloud (or an extension/application) to generate a correct RSS feed, rather than for AntennaPod to accommodate for ownclouds shortcomings.

Is there something wrong with the Owncloud RSS feed format?

Yes, there are a couple of missing tags. Just compare the resulting RSS feed with any other podcast feed. You can also use a [validator](http://castfeedvalidator.com/) to check for irregularities (although I'm not sure how good/bad this particular one is). Furthermore owncloud will export every activity to the feed, so non-media stuff will end up in there, too.

All of this should be tackled by owncloud and/or an appropriate application. In my opinion it makes absolutely no sense for AntennaPod to have dedicated logic to be able to parse owncloud's feeds. Once owncloud produces a "valid" podcast feed it can be used just like any other source with AntennaPod. Furthermore it could also be used with any other podcast-aware application. Such an approach sounds much more reasonable to me.

Ah ok, I don't have a sample Owncloud feed to look at but I know what you mean.

How about using a 3rd party service like https://feedsanitizer.appspot.com/ to consume the non-compliant source feed and output a standardized RSS?

Sanitizing the feed will not work. The feed itself is fine, but it is simply not meant to be used as source for podcasting applications in its current form. It misses some essential tags. Sanitizing it won't fix the issue.

Simply said: RSS feed != Podcast feed.

# Feature description

**Problem you may be having, or feature you want**:
Most podcasters do great work, and some users might want to support them. Since the removal of flattr AntennaPod has not have a function to support podcasters financially.

The Podcast Index has introduced a namespace to enrich the RSS standard. It introduces a new 'funding' tag, in which podcasters can provide links to payment options. [More specifications here.](https://www.github.com/Podcastindex-org/podcast-namespace/tree/main/docs%2F1.0.md#funding)

**Suggested solution**:
It would be great if we support this tag in its most basic form, meaning:
* On the podcast 'information' screen, add a 'Funding' title/section
* If the tag is not present, display the text "The creators have not indicated any way to financially support their work. If you want to donate, contact the podcast creator(s) and suggest them to include the [funding tag](https://github.com/Podcastindex-org/podcast-namespace/blob/main/docs/1.0.md#funding) in their RSS feed."
* If one or more tags is present, list each of the tags on one line. (They would be links that open in the phone's default browser.)

**Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details**:
* Tag: `<podcast:funding>`
* Parent: `<channel>`
* Attributes:
  * **url**: The URL to be followed to fund the podcast.
  * **platform (optional)**: Identifies a payment or funding platform for the podcast. Service slugs should be recorded here in the repository.
* Example: `<podcast:funding platform="paypal" url="www.paypal.me/myshow">Support the show!</podcast:funding>`

Or add the funding information in the show notes tab.
Funding seems to be related to the show, not an individual episode. I therefore think that it would be better to have this on the podcast info page than on the player screen (which is about an individual episode).
(Personally I feel like this feature request is the minimum we should do. But once that's implemented we can maybe think of ways to make if more prominent/convenient.)
By the way, there already is an existing [standard](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml) for dealing with payment URLs: `<link rel="payment" href="...">`. AntennaPod already parses and stores that one because it was used for Flattr support. It currently does not display the URL, though.

You mean the progress indicator in the toolbar when updating feeds, right?

On a technical level, the problem is that the ActionBar is set whenever loading a Fragment but not when resuming it. The update call to the ActionBar then gets lost (delivered to the child fragment). Instead, AntennaPod should use toolbars and update them directly. Updating the ActionBar in onResume is not a solution. Related: #4124

Ok i think i found the bug:
https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/8f6c560f01334c1fa0e74b05cbf1dbad05119572/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/fragment/EpisodesListFragment.java#L269
https://github.com/AntennaPod/AntennaPod/blob/8f6c560f01334c1fa0e74b05cbf1dbad05119572/app/src/main/java/de/danoeh/antennapod/fragment/AllEpisodesFragment.java#L101

When filtering, `AllEpisodesFragment.loadMoreData()` will return a `List<FeedItem>` with a `size()` smaller than the `EpisodesListFragment.EPISODES_PER_PAGE` as soon as the filter matches & removes entries from the result of `DBReader.getRecentlyPublishedEpisodes((page - 1) * EPISODES_PER_PAGE, EPISODES_PER_PAGE)`. As a result, the check `if (data.size() < EPISODES_PER_PAGE)` concludes that `hasMoreItems = false`, even though it isn't caused by a lack of additional database entries, but rather just the filter that removed unwanted entries from the database query result.
One possible solution i can think of right now:

Define the contract for `EpisodesListFragment.loadMoreData()` so that it must return `null` if there is no more data. That can be checked for in `EpisodesListFragment.loadMoreItems()` in place of `if (data.size() < EPISODES_PER_PAGE)`. Consequently, the `EpisodesListFragment.hasMoreItems` attribute would behave almost as it does right now, only that it should take exactly one extra round before the attribute gets changed.

To make implementations of the abstract `EpisodesListFragment.loadMoreData()` method keep up with the contract change, do the checking there. The existing `if (data.size() < EPISODES_PER_PAGE)` check could be moved straight into those implementations, along with a new attribute analogous to `EpisodesListFragment.hasMoreItems` keeping track of the state within those classes.

If we prolonged time when decreasing volume it should decrease slower. Right now when it is decreasing it becomes barely audible and it's quite annoying since you miss the latest seconds.
I think we need to come up with a good default without adding new options. In most cases, adding more and more options is bad for the user experience.

> Right now when it is decreasing it becomes barely audible and it's quite annoying since you miss the latest seconds.

The volume needs to be decreased enough so you can hear that the end is near (and that you need to shake the device to continue listening). Also, you need some seconds to grab the device and shake it, so less than 10 seconds seems pretty short to me. Volume currently goes to 10% at 10s. Maybe it should go to 50% at 10s and then to 20% at 5s.

Changing the volume smoothly will be pretty hard to integrate. Changing every second for the last 10 seconds could work and would be a lot more smooth than it currently is.

Feature Request: Add folder/directory as virtual podcast
I frequently transfer podcasts from my pc to my phone and it would be much appreciated if you could add an option in "Add a new feed" to select a local folder/directory to add as a sort of virtual podcast.

Allow addition of local files to queue
I mainly use AntennaPod to listen to podcasts I subscribed to, but from time to time I also listen to mp3 files I have on my SD card (an old podcast which closed but made all its archives available).

So I suggest the following feature: **allowing user to add local files to the queue**, these files being stored locally.
I see different ways to do this:
- Manually, the user would browse to a directory, then select one or several files to add to the queue (selecting several files should be possible).
- Allowing the addition of a new kind of feed by giving a local directory: AntennaPod would check this directory to see if files have been added, and then treat them as a classic feed.

I know it is possible to open a file with AntennaPod from the file manager, but this way does not allow one to build a listening list (the queue) with episodes both from classic feeds and from local files.

Database size optimization
I played around with a database export that has many subscriptions and therefore many feed items. The database is kind of huge, so we might want to make it smaller. I think we can reduce the size of the AntennaPod database by quite a bit by not storing unnecessary data.

| State | Size | Reason |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Original      | 71.2MB |  |
| Removed `FeedItems.payment_url` and `FeedItems.flattr_status` | 71.1MB | Both unused. |
| Removed `FeedItems.content_encoded` | 44.6MB | Descriptions are stored twice. We either display `content_encoded` or `description` but the database stores both. |
| `UPDATE FeedMedia SET mime_type = "@" WHERE mime_type == "audio/mpeg"` | 44.3MB | Most items have the same mime type. Instead of storing the type explicitly, we could have a small list of well-known types and store a reference instead. |
| Removed `Feeds.downloaded`  | 44.3MB | Does not look like it needs to be persisted. It is always 1. Only used while parsing the feed and in that case we just need a flag in the `Feed` object. |
| Removed `Feeds.hide` and `Feeds.payment_link`  | 44.3MB | Unused |
| Removed all download log entries except the newest 150 | 44.0MB | The list only displays 150 items |

According to `sqlite3_analyzer`, the tables `FeedItems` and `FeedMedia` need 98% of the file size.
